stories.headline: Six killed in Kraków shooting; three more bodies found at suspect’s home

sources.body:
Suspect was influenced by far-right ideology and held ‘ultra-nationalistic’ views, says Polish interior minister

Six people have been killed and 16 wounded after a gunman opened fire in a busy market square in Kraków, authorities said, in what Poland’s defence minister called an “act of terror” on the people of the city.

The suspect, a 25-year-old Polish citizen, opened fire with an automatic weapon in the city’s main square at about 3pm on Saturday.

He was fascinated with far-right ideologies and held “very radical” and “ultra-nationalistic” views, the Polish interior minister, Marcin Kierwiński, said at a news conference.

Four women and two men were killed, one of them a British citizen, Polish police said. Three of the victims were Polish women and the remaining two victims had not been identified.

The foreign nationals wounded were from Britain, Austria, Germany, Portugal and Russia, a Polish government spokesperson said.

The ⁠injured included two police ⁠officers, one of whom is in a serious condition after being shot three times in the exchange of fire with the alleged attacker.

Late on Saturday night, Poland’s prime minister, Donald Tusk, said two more women and one man had also been found dead in the suspect’s home, most likely members of his family, he added.

The Polish defense minister, Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz, called Saturday’s fatal shooting an “act of terror” on the people of Krakow, Poland’s second-largest city, which receives 15 million visitors a year, most of them passing through the main square.

A tram driver reported about 3pm that his vehicle was shot at from a man in a moving car while passing nearby the main square, the Krakow municipal transport company said. The window to the tram driver’s cabin was shattered.

On Saturday evening, government spokesperson Adam Szłapka wrote on X: “Today’s event in Kraków has shaken all of Poland,” adding that Tusk was “on his way to Kraków”

A digest of the morning's main headlines from the Europe edition emailed direct to you every week day

The justice minister, Waldemar Żurek, wrote on X that authorities would “ensure that the perpetrator of this crime is held fully accountable and severely punished”.

The Polish president, Karol Nawrocki, said he was “deeply concerned by reports of the tragic events” in Kraków, and that his thoughts are with victims, those injured and their families.

Earlier this year, Euronews reported that the number of legally owned firearms in Poland surpassed 1m for the first time.

Poland issued a record 50,700 gun permits in 2025, and the number of active permits registered in 2025 was almost double the number registered in 2015, according to the police statistics cited in the report.

Sunday and Monday will be a period of national mourning for the victims of the attack.
sources.headline: Six dead after gunman opens fire in Kraków market square, with three more victims found at suspect’s home

sources.body: A chilling new discovery in Poland, where three bodies have reportedly been found inside the Krakow gunman's home. That's in addition to six people killed and sixteen wounded when the attacker opened fire in the city's historic square. Prime Minister Donald Tusk has now declared the shooting an act of terrorism, saying Poland has never experienced anything quite like it. The 25-year-old suspect, described by authorities as holding radical far-right views, was shot by police.
sources.headline: Gunmen kills six in Krakow, three more bodies found at his house

sources.body:
The suspect, a Polish national, has been arrested after the shooting that also injured 15.

At least six people have been killed and 15 others wounded, including police officers and foreign nationals, in a shooting in the centre of Krakow in southern Poland.

Police said that a man drove onto the city’s Main Market Square at about 3pm (14:00 GMT) on Saturday and “began firing at random people from his car”. Four women and two men were killed.

Police said officers shot and detained the man, who acted alone. He has since been transported to hospital to receive treatment for his injuries.

A British national was among those killed, according to Polish police chief Marek Boron, and five foreigners were among the wounded in hospital. Boron said two of the victims had not yet been identified. The authorities have not disclosed the nationalities of all the victims.

The Ministry of the Interior confirmed that the suspect is a Polish citizen, with Interior Minister Marcin Kierwinski saying he appeared to be “fascinated by far-right ideologies” and held “ultra-nationalist views”.

“During the arrest, officers used their weapons, but the man returned fire; as a result, two police officers are among the injured,” a police spokesperson said.

Kierwinski said that one of the police officers is in a critical condition. He also said that five foreigners were among the wounded hospitalised victims, and one foreign national was among those killed.

Kierwinski said a number of weapons were found in the car the suspect was driving.

According to police, the man was wearing military-style attire and used a semi-automatic rifle similar to a US AR-15.

In a post on X, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk praised the “heroic” police response to the “tragic shooting”.

Tusk later told reporters in Krakow the shooting was an act of “terrorism”.

“Until now in Poland, we haven’t had such drastic cases of terrorism,” he said, adding: “That’s what we have to call this cruel attack on people’s lives here in Krakow.”

He announced two days of national mourning and said three bodies – two women and a man – had been found at the suspect’s home, with “much to suggest that they are members of the [suspect’s] immediate family”.

“I am being kept informed by the Minister of the Interior about the situation in Krakow,” he wrote on X, adding that “the police are investigating the background and all the circumstances of the attack”.

President Karol Nawrocki said his thoughts were with the victims, those affected, and their families.

Nawrocki said he was awaiting “a full explanation of the circumstances surrounding these dramatic events”, adding that the safety of Poles was “an absolute priority”.

Minister of Foreign Affairs Radoslaw Sikorski said on social media that he was “receiving dozens of messages from foreign ministers from all over the world offering their condolences”.

Tom Rose, the US ambassador to Poland, called the incident a “horrific mass shooting … a savage and murderous attack that’s shattered the peace of Poland”.
sources.headline: At least six people killed in shooting in Poland’s Krakow main square

stories.headline: Israel’s president asks Netanyahu rival Gadi Eisenkot to form a government

sources.body:
Knesset has been deadlocked since the election last month when Benjamin Netanyahu’s coalition lost its majority

Israel’s president has ⁠chosen Gadi Eisenkot, prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s ⁠strongest rival, to ⁠try to ​form a new government, after a deadlocked election that left neither man ⁠with a clear path to power.

Isaac Herzog’s office said he had informed Eisenkot, the leader of the Yashar party, on Saturday night “of his intention to task him with forming a government”.

It added that the formal appointment would take place in an official ceremony on Sunday at the president’s residence in Jerusalem.

“Now is the time to form a national emergency government. I will do everything to ensure we are worthy,” Eisenkot wrote on X in his first reaction to the announcement of his designation.

Netanyahu ‌is fighting to hold on to office ‌after his religious-nationalist coalition lost its majority in an election on 27 October but still emerged as the largest bloc ‌in parliament.

Should Eisenkot succeed in forming a coalition, he would take over as prime minister from Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving premier.

Eisenkot’s wide-ranging opposition bloc won 48 of the Israeli parliament’s 120 seats in October elections, while Netanyahu’s camp secured 53, leaving neither with a majority.

During party consultations with Herzog, 66-year-old Eisenkot received the endorsements of both Arab-majority lists, who could now play kingmakers after making unprecedented gains in the vote.

But it remains unclear if Eisenkot’s bloc would accept support from the Arab lists in forming a government.

Eisenkot, the military chief of staff from 2015 to 2019, has set out to unite Israelis after Netanyahu’s divisive tenure, under which the country moved sharply to the right.

He has vowed to crack down on extremist West Bank settlers who have attacked Palestinians with impunity, decrying recent incidents as “Jewish terror” abetted by Netanyahu’s government.

But the military man is no peacenik. He opposes the creation of a Palestinian state and vowed to end Hamas’s rule in Gaza and destroy the Islamist movement’s military wing.

Commanding the military during the 2006 war with Hezbollah, Eisenkot devised the so-called “Dahiya doctrine”. The idea, named after a Beirut suburb heavily damaged in that war, involves Israel vowing to use massive force against civilian infrastructure in areas controlled by the Lebanese militant movement Hezbollah.

After his appointment, Eisenkot will have 28 days to come up with the 61 votes needed for a government. If he comes up short, Herzog can provide a 14-day extension before he has to offer the mandate to someone else.

If neither side succeeds, Israel will head to fresh elections. The country held five elections between 2019 and 2022 due to repeated deadlocks.
sources.headline: Israel’s president picks Yashar leader Gadi Eisenkot to form government

sources.body:
Former army chief has 28 days to build a coalition that would end Benjamin Netanyahu’s long tenure as prime minister.

Israel’s President Isaac Herzog has tasked Gadi Eisenkot with forming the country’s next government, passing over the former army chief’s rival, Benjamin Netanyahu.

Herzog told Eisenkot of his decision on Saturday evening and will formally hand him the mandate at a ceremony on Sunday, the president’s spokesperson said.

Herzog held consultations with political parties this week to decide who he would appoint to form a government after neither side secured a majority in the October 27 general election.

Some 67 lawmakers, including from Arab-led parties, endorsed Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party, to form the next government, while only 46 backed Netanyahu, the current prime minister.

Eisenkot will have 28 days – with a possible 14-day extension – to build a coalition of at least 61 of the Knesset’s 120 seats, the minimum threshold for a government.

In the October election, Eisenkot’s four-party alliance won 48 seats, while Netanyahu’s right-wing and religious bloc secured 53, leaving both short of the 61 needed for a parliamentary majority. Arab-led parties, representing Palestinian citizens of Israel, won a record 19 seats.

Eisenkot has ruled out forming a government with the Arab-led parties, which would give him a 67-seat bloc. Winning over the two ultra-Orthodox parties, United Torah Judaism and Shas, would give him exactly 61 seats.

He could also form a government with fewer than 61 seats if he wins a parliamentary confidence vote.

Al Jazeera’s Nour Odeh, reporting from Ramallah in the occupied West Bank on Herzog’s decision, said the president “took the predictable route” in selecting Eisenkot, as he had the highest number of recommendations.

“The hard work will begin now for Eisenkot to put together a government that can pass a vote of confidence at the Knesset that: one, will not break too many of the promises he made on the campaign trail; and two, that can survive the opposition of the right-wing bloc led by Netanyahu,” Odeh said.

If Eisenkot fails to form a government within the allotted time, Herzog will nominate another candidate. If the second nominee fails, a parliament majority can back a third candidate, who will be granted a final 14 days.

If, once again, no government is formed, a new election will be called within 90 days, with Netanyahu staying on as a caretaker prime minister.

Eisenkot led Israel’s military from 2015 to 2019 and sat as an observer in Netanyahu’s war cabinet for the first eight months of Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza, which began in October 2023.

Ahmad Tibi, a senior member of the Joint List – a coalition of Arab-led parties that holds 11 seats – told Al Jazeera on Saturday that Herzog’s decision was “expected”.

“We were concerned that the president would move towards a national unity government,” he said, referring to a proposed power-sharing agreement between Eisenkot and Netanyahu.

Instead, Arab-led parties endorsed Eisenkot for the mandate, granting him a “considerable margin”.
sources.headline: Israel’s president picks Eisenkot over Netanyahu to form next government

stories.headline: US launches task force to disrupt Iran’s land supply routes

sources.body:
The operation is to prevent Iran from using ground routes to transport weapons and other materials, US Central Command says.

The United States military’s Central Command (CENTCOM) has announced a plan to block Iran’s land-based supply routes, expanding its months-long naval blockade of Iranian ports in the Strait of Hormuz.

CENTCOM, which oversees US military operations in the Middle East, announced on Saturday that it had established a new task force “to prevent Iran from using ground routes to transport advanced weapons and other materials”.

Task Force Iron Gate will reinforce “the success of our ironclad blockade against Iran at sea”, CENTCOM Commander Admiral Brad Cooper said.

Based in Tampa, Florida, the task force will coordinate with other US government agencies “on preventing the movement of advanced weapons systems, dual-use technologies, sanctioned materials, and illegal revenue streams across Iran’s land borders and the Caspian Sea”, CENTCOM said.

Michael Mulroy, a former US deputy assistant defence secretary for the Middle East, told Al Jazeera the task force’s role will be to find out where “weapons systems are coming in, how they could potentially be cut off”, and how “Iran is transporting its energy”.

He added that if US President Donald Trump orders an escalation to the war, it will likely be attacks on this “series of targets”.

“Unlike Operation Epic Fury , which primarily focuses on military targets, I think these targets will be focused on economic and infrastructure targets, as part of this comprehensive plan to cut the regime off from its ability to fight and ability to fund itself,” Mulroy told Al Jazeera.

CENTCOM separately said on Saturday that it had disabled a commercial cargo vessel in the Gulf of Oman as part of its blockade of Iranian ports.

A US “military aircraft fired precision munitions at the stern of St. Kitts-flagged M/V Huda, disabling the ship after CENTCOM forces directed the crew to abandon targeted spaces”, it said in a statement.

“Enforcement actions since July have resulted in U.S. forces redirecting 147 commercial vessels that complied”, and disabling “five merchant ships that refused to comply”, it added.

On Saturday, Iran’s official news agency IRNA reported the sound of two explosions on Qeshm Island, located in the Strait of Hormuz.

IRNA also reported the sound of “several explosions” in the cities of Jask, Sirik and Bandar Abbas.

Trump confirmed new strikes on Qeshm Island a day earlier, but downplayed them as “minor”. He added that Tehran still wants a deal as Qatari-mediated talks continue.

Meanwhile, Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy reported that two oil tankers struck mines near the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday.

Iranian state television, citing the navy, said the tankers had passed through an “unsafe” part of the strait with their navigation systems off. They “suffered severe damage and stopped after hitting sea mines”.
sources.headline: US launches task force to disrupt Iran’s land-based supply routes

stories.headline: Russian strikes leave Kyiv facing power and water shortages ahead of talks

sources.body:
Moscow used 172 drones and 36 ballistic missiles in attacks on electricity substations and bridge over the Dnipro

Volodymyr Zelenskyy has accused Russia of trying to “plunge Kyiv and the entire country into a blackout”, after a major attack overnight on energy infrastructure in the capital and a bridge over the Dnipro River.

Ukraine’s president said Moscow’s preparations for peace talks next week involved pummelling a city of millions with ballistic missiles.

Negotiators from Russia , Ukraine and the US are due to meet on Tuesday and Wednesday in Abu Dhabi, the capital of the United Arab Emirates, for talks aimed at ending the war.

Zelenskyy appealed to the US Congress – won by the Democrats in the midterm elections – to pay more attention to Ukraine in the face of relentless Russian bombardment. “Ukraine must not be left alone. We are counting on increased bilateral support from the US,” he said .

Russia used 172 drones and 36 ballistic missiles in its latest attack on Kyiv and surrounding regions. The city faced serious difficulties with its electricity, water and heat supplies, Zelenskyy said, with five people injured including a 14-year-old girl.

The strikes targeted substations in five regions, including one connecting two nuclear power plants to Kyiv. The city’s Northern Bridge, a key transport artery, was closed on Saturday as workers repaired damage to the road’s surface and power lines.

The attacks cap a dire week for residents in Kyiv, who have experienced day-long power cuts and interruptions to the water supply. Ukrainian officials say the Kremlin’s goal is to freeze civilians into submission over the brutal winter months, a war crime.

They have little confidence that US-backed peace talks will yield concrete results. In an interview with CNN , Zelenskyy described the latest blueprint set out by Jared Kushner, Donald Trump’s son-in-law, as “Yalta 2.0” – a reference to the 1945 summit between Stalin, Roosevelt and Churchill that divided postwar Europe.

In a series of social media posts , Kushner said the discussions would include a new security framework for Europe, alongside guarantees for Ukraine. This appears to be a reference to the Kremlin’s longstanding demand that Nato’s expansion across Europe be reversed.

A digest of the morning's main headlines from the Europe edition emailed direct to you every week day

Speaking on Friday, Trump said a “big beautiful agreement” could be close, involving “all of Europe”. Shortly before invading Ukraine, the Russian president, Vladimir Putin, demanded that Nato go back to its pre-1997 posture – before the Baltic states and nations in eastern Europe and the Balkans joined.

Ukraine and its European partners are deeply sceptical. “The idea of discussing European-Russian security infrastructure is not simple, and it can be dangerous,” Zelenskyy told CNN, emphasising: “We don’t want to be divided by Russia.”

Zelenskyy said Moscow had to end its war first, with Ukraine given meaningful security guarantees. After that, “depending on the answers”, wider security architecture could be considered, he said. Western diplomats say agreeing to Russia’s demands would effectively end Nato.
sources.headline: Blackouts and water shortages in Kyiv after Russia strikes Ukraine’s energy grid

sources.body: As Ukraine prepares for another round of talks with Russia and the United States next week, Moscow has launched a massive overnight strike. At least five people were injured in Kyiv, where Russian missiles damaged residential and commercial buildings, forced the closure of a bridge over the Dnipro River and caused fresh power and water outages. Ophélie Jacobson reports.
sources.headline: Russia launches massive strike on Kyiv

stories.headline: New Zealand election is too close to call, with weeks of coalition talks likely

sources.body:
National party will be largest in parliament but ultimate shape of next government won’t be settled for some time

New Zealand could be facing a weeks-long wait to know the shape of its next government, after its nail-biting election failed to hand a decisive victory to either the incumbent rightwing coalition or opposition left bloc.

On preliminary results, the centre-right National party, led by the prime minister, Christopher Luxon , managed to secure enough seats to govern alongside its traditional coalition partners, the libertarian Act and populist New Zealand First parties.

But with some seats won by very slim margins, and special votes yet to be counted, that success is precarious, resulting in an election too close to call until official results are released on 27 November.

Special votes include overseas votes and ballots cast outside a voter’s electorate. In 2023, 600,000 such votes were made, 21% of the total. These votes tend to favour the left – in 2023, special votes resulted in Te Pāti Māori (the Māori party) and the Greens gaining three seats between them.

With nearly 100% of the regular votes counted on Saturday night, National secured 42 seats, Act 13 and New Zealand First 12. The combined 67-seat majority is wafer thin, with the left bloc just three seats behind.

Speaking to a room full of the party faithful at Auckland’s Viaduct events centre just before midnight, Luxon said the results were “too close to call” and the special votes would need to be counted before negotiations could begin.

National was still the largest party in parliament, he said, and had “a pathway to forming the next government”. National pipped Labour by 0.02% in the party vote.

Labour, led by Chris Hipkins , secured 35 seats, while its traditional coalition partners the Greens won 16 and Te Pāti Māori five. Even with the seven seats from the centrist newcomer party, Opportunity, the left bloc is three seats short of forming a government.

Before a rowdy crowd of supporters at the Cosmopolitan Club in Upper Hutt, north of Wellington, Hipkins joked that New Zealand had spoken but “it may take a bit longer to work out what they’ve said”.

“As things stand tonight, it is clear that we are not going to know the shape of our next government for a little while longer yet,” Hipkins said, promising that Labour would get “straight to work” should the final count land in its favour.

The collapse of the two major parties, amid a sluggish economy and stubbornly high ⁠inflation, is feeding record support for the smaller parties, including Act, New Zealand First and the Greens. It is also helped propel Opportunity into parliament for the first time.

Opinion polls in the lead-up to the election had Opportunity placed to become the kingmaker. At this stage, the right bloc does not need the party to govern, but if special votes change the landscape, its predicted role could come to fruition.

Currently at 5.9%, the centrist party has met the threshold needed to enter parliament, a historic first. Since New Zealand adopted the mixed-member proportional (MMP) electoral system in 1996, no new party has been able to meet that threshold – all the other minor parties have been born from MPs or groups splintering from larger parties.
sources.headline: New Zealand faces weeks of uncertainty with election ‘too close to call’

sources.body:
Thanks for following the blog tonight. The election has ended without a clear winner. Here are the top news lines from what will go down as one of New Zealand’s closest elections in many decades .

Christopher Luxon’s National party and its right-leaning coalition partners are on the brink of a wafer-thin majority that could allow it to eke out a return to power.

The left-wing bloc, led by Labour’s Chris Hipkins, fell short of a majority .

Neither Luxon or Hipkins claimed victory or conceded defeat . Both acknowledged an expected wait before a governing coalition is negotiated.

A centrist newcomer, the Opportunity party, has entered parliament, polling above the 5% threshold . They could potentially be a kingmaker in a coalition.

Final results are expected on 27 November . Coalition talks will likely take weeks.

Hundreds of thousands of special votes are yet to be counted and could change the shape of parliament .

Saturday figures showed there could be a 130-seat parliament , with 66 seats needed for a majority.

Results suggested a coalition of National, Act and NZ First would hold 67 seats.

The 67 included 42 for National, 13 for Act and 12 for NZ First.

The left-bloc totalled 56 seats: Labour 35, Greens 16 and 5 for Te Pāti Māori.

Opportunity is projected to gain 7 seats.
sources.headline: New Zealand election coalition talks will likely take weeks – as it happened

stories.headline: More than 30 reportedly killed in Yemen market attack as responsibility is disputed

sources.body: At least 30 people have reportedly been killed in an attack on a market in Yemen’s Taiz province, with Houthi rebels blaming Saudi airstrikes. Government forces and local authorities have disputed the claim, instead accusing the Houthis of indiscriminate fire. The province has witnessed intense clashes in recent weeks and is home to around half of the more than 300,000 people displaced by the latest fighting. Caroline Baum reports.
sources.headline: Yemen: 30 dead in strikes on Taiz market

sources.body:
Civilians bear the brunt of fighting as 27 people reported killed in strikes on a village in Sanaa province.

Yemeni government forces say they have repelled Houthi assaults in Marib, as the armed group said strikes on a village in Sanaa province had killed at least 27 people.

In a statement on Saturday, government forces said troops backed by warplanes and drones had fought for hours to halt Houthi advances in Marib province, destroying fortifications and combat equipment.

It said troops were also pushing into Houthi-held areas of al-Jawf province, where fighting entered a third consecutive day as part of the “Dawn of Yemen” operation launched more than a month ago by the internationally recognised government, to take control of territory from Houthi fighters.

In a separate statement, government forces spokesman, Colonel Majed al-Nazili, said the army had carried out 875 attacks on Houthi positions on Saturday, “neutralising” about 130 Houthi commanders and fighters and destroying or disabling 50 vehicles and missile launchers.

Al Jazeera could not independently verify the claims.

Also on Saturday, a series of strikes killed at least 27 people and wounded about 30 others in Sanaa province, the Houthi-run ⁠Saba news ⁠agency reported.

Anees al-Asbahi, a spokesman for the Sanaa-based Ministry of Health, said the attacks struck al-Shariya village, north of the capital. He said most of the casualties were women and children.

The Iran-backed Houthis – also known as Ansar Allah, Arabic for Supporters of God – blamed the Saudi-led coalition supporting Yemen’s government forces for the attack. The President of the armed group’s Supreme Political Council, Field Marshal Mahdi al-Mashat, vowed to “avenge” the attack.

Al Jazeera could not independently verify the reports. Saudi Arabia and the Yemeni government have not commented on the reported strikes.

The incident comes a day after the Houthis and Yemen’s government traded blame over a separate attack that killed civilians at a market in Taiz.

Reporting from Sanaa, Al Jazeera’s Yousef Mawry said the Houthis put the civilian death toll from the past two days at 55, blaming Saudi air strikes, while Yemeni government officials have held the Houthis responsible for most of the casualties.

“Two narratives are blaming each other and pointing the finger at each other, while this is taking a toll on civilian casualties,” Mawry said.

As fighting continues in Yemen, the Houthis separately claimed to have launched six attacks on Saudi targets using ballistic and cruise missiles and drones, but did not say when the attacks were carried out.

The group said it had targeted King Khalid international airport and oil facilities in Riyadh, an oil site in Khurais, an oil pumping station in Dawadmi, a National Guard camp in Najran and what it described as Saudi troop gatherings in Yemen’s al-Jawf and Marib provinces.

Colonel Turki al-Malki, spokesman for the Saudi-backed coalition supporting Yemen’s government forces, said early on Saturday that they had shot down a Houthi ballistic missile over the Riyadh region.
sources.headline: Yemeni gov’t forces report advances as Houthis say deadly strikes hit Sanaa

stories.headline: Trump calls for Justice Department investigation into Democratic oversight plans

sources.body: In this new era of divided government, Democratic lawmakers say their priorities will be tackling the rising cost of living, investigating alleged corruption and tightening oversight of ICE agents. Antonia Kerrigan reports.
sources.headline: USA: Democrats vow to investigate Donald Trump

stories.headline: Trump asks UFC chief Dana White to become White House press secretary

sources.body: US President Donald Trump on Saturday said he was asking mixed martial arts promoter Dana White to be the new White House press secretary. Trump has repeatedly tried to hitch his MAGA brand of politics to White's enormously successful Ultimate Fighting Championship.
sources.headline: 'A violent fighter and warrior': Trump offers press secretary role to UFC chief Dana White

sources.body:
Ultimate Fighting Championship CEO says he will meet with the US president on Monday to discuss the offer.

Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) chief executive Dana White has said he will meet with Donald Trump after the US president offered him the job of White House press secretary.

Speaking at a new conference after a boxing event in London on Saturday, White said he would meet with Trump at the White House on Monday to discuss the president’s offer.

“Dana will be a Press Secretary like none other,” Trump wrote on Truth Social earlier on Saturday. “Dana, please take the job!”

Trump also requested that White “bring with him assistants, even though some are not from our Country”.

Trump listed and posted pictures of six current and former UFC title holders to join White: Islam Makhachev and Khabib Nurmagomedov from Russia’s Dagestan region; Americans Justin Gaethje, Daniel Cormier and “Kayla Harris”, likely a reference to Kayla Harrison; and Amanda Nunes, a Brazilian who became a US citizen last year.

“We need these people to defend us against the Lunatic Left,” Trump wrote.

The White House press secretary role has been vacant since Katie Zacharia’s tenure ended ‌last ⁠month after just five days.

Zacharia succeeded Karoline Leavitt, who stepped down from the role at the end of August.

White and Trump first worked together in the early 2000s, but they grew closer since ⁠the UFC chief publicly backed Trump’s presidential campaign in 2016.

In recent years, Trump has attended several UFC events, and in June, the White House hosted a night of UFC fights as ⁠part of celebrations marking the 250th anniversary of US independence.

The White House press office already has a former UFC spokesperson among its ranks: Director of Communications ⁠Steven Cheung, who worked for White’s organisation from 2013 to 2016.

Cheung shared the president’s message on X and said, “Hell yeah! Do it, @DanaWhite! It’ll just be like old times!”
sources.headline: Trump asks UFC chief Dana White to be White House press secretary

stories.headline: AI stocks fall as investors weigh prospects for tighter oversight and slower data center growth

sources.body: Investors are worried that data center building will slow. If the AI industry’s investment math no longer works, the U.S. economy could take a hit.
sources.headline: Why investors are dumping AI company stocks after Democrats’ election sweep

sources.body:
Asian and European markets follow US tech rout with many analysts predicting more waves of selling to come

European and Asian stock markets fell sharply on Friday after the Democrats’ decisive victory in the midterms triggered a rout in US tech stocks a day earlier.

A sell-off on Wall Street on Thursday was followed by sharp falls in Asian stock markets on Friday. The investor sentiment then reached London, where the market was, at one stage, poised for its worst day since March.

The FTSE 100 index, which tracks blue-chip shares listed in London, was down as much as 254 points, or 2.35%, at 10,528 points during a wave of selling in morning trading. But by the close of the day it had clawed back some of its losses to be down 1%, helped by a rise in US stocks when Wall Street reopened.

Germany’s Dax index fell by 2%, France’s Cac 40 dropped by 0.8% and Spain’s Ibex lost 0.6%.

Susannah Streeter, the chief investment strategist at Wealth Club, said: “The tech sell-off has intensified, with the pain of the brutal sell-off on Wall Street carried straight through to Asia and knocking sentiment in Europe .

“Big worries are colliding – the build-out of datacentres looks set to slow, which risks shredding the spending spree underpinning the boom, right at the time that investors have become super nervous about returns on this massive investment.”

However, there were signs of easing jitters on Wall Street on Friday, where tech stocks rose, lifting the S&P 500 share index by 0.3% and the tech-heavy Nasdaq closed up 1% – which only recovered a portion of their previous day’s losses.

That followed a stronger-than-expected employment report that showed the US economy added 165,000 new jobs in October, pulling the unemployment rate down to 4.1%.

On Thursday, the Nasdaq share index had its worst day in 19 months after slumping 5.5%.

Chip stocks led the slump on Thursday, with the memory maker SanDisk tumbling by 22% and the hard drive maker Western Digital falling by 17%. Wall Street’s “fear index”, the Vix, jumped by more than 60% to its highest levels since the early weeks of the Iran war, in a sign of rising market volatility.

The heavy falls continued in Asia on Friday, with Japan’s Nikkei 225 index sinking 6% and South Korea’s Kospi index tumbling more than 6.5%.

“It’s actually a bit of a disaster,” said Christopher Forbes, the head of Asia and Middle East at CMC Markets.

“[Clients] were long index, long stocks, and they all got carried out. All night, all day – we had client margin calls, client complaints … because it’s a very emotional thing, right? People are wedded to their positions and views on a stock or outcome, and you’re telling them: ‘Look, you’ve just lost money.’”

Chris Beauchamp, the chief market analyst at the investing and trading platform IG, said: “Yesterday’s [Thursday’s] brutal session marked a dramatic turnaround from Wednesday, but with AI fears still prominent there is a risk that there is much more selling to come.

Get set for the working day – we'll point you to all the business news and analysis you need every morning
sources.headline: Global stocks fall amid ‘big worries over AI’ after Democrats’ midterms triumph

sources.body: Democrats are also calling for tighter regulation of AI data centres, a concern shared across Europe. In Amsterdam, several hundred activists occupied the site of a planned Microsoft data centre as part of a two-day protest taking place across the continent. Jennie Shin reports.
sources.headline: AI Data centres face growing backlash

sources.body: <p>La <a href="https://elpais.com/noticias/huelgas-generales/" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/noticias/huelgas-generales/">huelga general</a> del próximo miércoles es, desde múltiples puntos de vista, inédita. Parte de la iniciativa de un movimiento sin capacidad legal para convocarla, el Sindicato de Inquilinas (SDI), y no de los sindicatos de clase tradicionales, UGT y CC OO, que se han sumado a esa reclamación y han sido los que han “legalizado” la convocatoria, explica Valeria Racu, portavoz del SDI. No tiene que ver con cuestiones estrictamente laborales, sino, sobre todo, con las dificultades de acceso a la vivienda. La ministra de Trabajo, Yolanda Díaz, ha animado a la población a participar en ella —“Creo que va a ser la primera vez que no puedo ir de piquete. Bien que me gustaría”, dijo—; el líder de la oposición, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, ha pedido a los sindicatos que la desconvoquen —“Las huelgas generales no se convocan contra quien no gobierna”—; y la última fue hace 14 años, en 2012, contra los recortes del Ejecutivo de Mariano Rajoy. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-08/motivos-y-riesgos-de-una-huelga-general-atipica-que-pretende-marcar-un-antes-y-un-despues.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

sources.body: 450 persones, segons la Guàrdia Urbana, s’han manifestat aquest dissabte al vespre, a quatre dies de la vaga general de l’11 de novembre , “contra l’encariment de la vida” davant del Mercat de Sant Antoni. Convocats per l’Organització Juvenil Socialista (OJS), la protesta vol reunir tot el jovent que pateix el preu de l’habitatge, la manca de perspectives de futur, l’estancament dels salaris i la degradació dels serveis bàsics. “Darrere d’aquesta situació insostenible hi ha uns responsables clars: els rendistes que viuen a costa del nostre salari els empresaris que ens exploten i els governs que vetllen perquè així sigui”, ha assegurat Judith Gonzàlez, portaveu de l’OJS. També et pot interessar Manifestació per la vaga general de l’11 de novembre: horari, lloc i manifest Clara Aliaguilla 2 minuts de lectura Al·legat socialista “Existeix una generació que estem disposats a lluitar” contra el sistema, ha declarat una de les manifestants en una protesta en què han mostrat una pancarta amb el lema “Lluitem pel socialisme”. Una altra de les participants ha dit: “El socialisme és l’única via per construir una societat democràtica” . El col·lectiu també ha defensat la convocatòria d’una manifestació alternativa aquest 11-N per la vaga general. També et pot interessar El Sindicat d’Habitatge Socialista i Solidaritat Obrera faran una manifestació alternativa l’11-N Redacció 1 minut de lectura Des de la convocatòria de vaga general, la militància de l’OJS ha treballat en els més de 60 comitès d’arreu de Catalunya, ha impulsat i participat en els comitès universitaris i ha organitzat assemblees obertes amb els estudiants dels instituts.

Lo que en ningún caso contempla es pedir la abstención del PSOE para gobernar sin Vox:</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-08/alberto-nunez-feijoo-hacer-una-coalicion-de-gobierno-con-vox-no-depende-de-mi.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p><img src="https://imagenes.elpais.com/resizer/v2/FEZI3E3UIJFTLCHBYO6FZ3UWLM.jpg?auth=eb5387e3e3d8e3e1328ed6a5c2f9efea69fa33402ebad0ecab039d0f6e5c0f46" width="6586" height="4546" alt="Alberto Núñez Feijoo, posa en la sede de Génova del PP."></img><img src="https://imagenes.elpais.com/resizer/v2/JBBHIOZULRCMXOL3SX34OIG3UQ.jpg?auth=9eb876edb4ab24d5c1a1e5927f12e920c15d0c8e12b104740c8c37d15a7fdcd9" width="8192" height="5464" alt="Alberto Núñez Feijoo, durante la entrevista."></img><img src="https://imagenes.elpais.com/resizer/v2/AOAUGX6HLVA6RMDATOLCBBIV6I.jpg?auth=431df7023fe11a9e28149251733650f9a602bc7f0c69f92bf6d00a2a5dc88388" width="8192" height="5464" alt="Alberto Núñez Feijoo, durante la entrevista."></img>

stories.headline: El Hierro declares migration emergency after more than 8,000 arrivals in five weeks

sources.body:
Vista de las personas migrantes rescatadas este sábado, en dos cayucos, por Salvamento Marítimo, en aguas cercanas a El Hierro, y trasladadas a puerto para ser atendidas por los equipos de emergencia

El Cabildo de El Hierro ha declarado la emergencia social y la necesidad de colaboración con las instituciones superiores para la gestión de la actual crisis migratoria en la isla, con la llegada de más de 8.000 personas en las últimas cinco semanas. Entre la pasada medianoche y la mañana de este sábado, un total de 314 personas que viajaban en tres cayucos han desembarcado en El Hierro, informaron a Efe fuentes del dispositivo de emergencia.

Alpidio Armas, presidente del Cabildo, ha formalizado mediante decreto esta petición ante una situación que “se ha ido agravando en los últimos días, ejerciendo presión en los diferentes recursos tanto humanos como asistenciales con los que se cuenta en el protocolo”.

Solo en los últimos cinco días se han registrado más de 3.000 personas a bordo de una treintena de cayucos, detalla el Cabildo en una nota.

El presidente insular considera que estas cifras obligan a tomar esta decisión institucional para dar una respuesta acorde a la situación de forma “coordinada con el resto de las instituciones, porque El Hierro no puede afrontar esto solo”.

“Necesitamos más recursos y más medios para evitar que el protocolo que hemos venido realizando durante estos últimos años no se desborde ni se rompa”, comenta.

En este decreto se solicita tanto al Gobierno de Canarias como al Estado la presencia de más medios humanos y una rotación que permita el descanso al personal de los dispositivos de asistencia tanto de Salvamento Marítimo, como el Servicio Canario de la Salud, los Cuerpos y Fuerzas de Seguridad del Estado, Cruz Roja y otras ONG encargadas de la asistencia a personas migrantes.

En esta declaración también se contempla establecer protocolos para trasladar de forma coordinada a las personas migrantes a otras islas con mayor capacidad y reforzar las instalaciones de primera acogida de la isla, entre otras medidas.

El presidente también pone el acento en la necesidad de tener en cuenta la realidad de La Restinga y de los sectores que desarrollan su actividad en el entorno del puerto.

La situación migratoria tiene una “incidencia directa” en la dinámica habitual de esta localidad, por lo que resulta necesario atender también las necesidades de sus vecinos, comerciantes, empresas, profesionales del sector pesquero y empresas de buceo, señala Armas.

El Cabildo considera fundamental que las medidas que se adopten permitan compatibilizar la atención humanitaria con el normal desarrollo de la actividad de este pueblo pesquero.

Desde la corporación insular se solicita este tipo de medidas ante una situación que atraviesa El Hierro, que presenta ya un nivel de “tensión considerable”, al que se suma una “preocupación creciente” por las dificultades de coordinación y por el funcionamiento de los protocolos establecidos, que deben ofrecer respuestas ágiles y eficaces ante episodios de elevada afluencia.
sources.headline: El Hierro declara la emergencia migratoria ante la llegada de 8.000 migrantes

sources.body:
El Hierro asks Spanish government for help after more than 3,300 people arrived on boats since start of November.

Authorities of El Hierro, one of Spain’s Canary Islands, have declared an emergency and asked the government in Madrid for help after a surge in migrants and refugees arriving on boats.

“We are very concerned… by this sharp increase in arrivals,” Alpidio Armas, head of the governing council for El Hierro, one of Europe’s main entry points for migrants and refugees from West Africa, told Spanish television on Saturday.

“This is precisely what has led us to declare an emergency in order to ensure a framework of cooperation with higher-level institutions.”

More than 3,300 people have arrived on the island in about 30 boats since the start of November, according to local authorities. El Hierro has about 11,400 residents.

Officials are seeking temporary accommodation for the new arrivals, while conditions at the island’s hospital have become “undesirable”, Armas said.

The situation is “ absolutely unsustainable ”, the Reuters news agency quoted Fernando Clavijo, the regional leader of the Canary Islands, as saying on Friday.

Maritime rescue services rescued 3,261 migrants and refugees off the coast of the Canary Islands in the first six days of November.

Clavijo said the numbers were approaching the record levels seen in 2024, and on some days, the current pace was even higher.

Buses have been diverted to migration operations, and medical staff have been brought in from other islands, he said.

The Atlantic route from West Africa to the Canary Islands is one of the world’s deadliest migration crossings.

Two people were found dead on a boat heading for the Canaries this week, and five others are believed to have died during the voyage, according to the AFP news agency, citing survivor accounts.

At least nine migrants or refugees have died off the islands in recent weeks.

Arrivals reached a record of more than 46,000 in 2024, then fell sharply due to tighter surveillance and greater cooperation with countries of origin and transit.

Between January and October, 13,327 irregular migrants and refugees arrived by sea, 5.5 percent fewer than in the same period last year, according to Spain’s Ministry of the Interior.

Patrols off Senegal, Mauritania and Morocco have pushed departures further south, from The Gambia, Guinea-Bissau and Guinea, making crossings longer.

Senegalese police said on Saturday that they intercepted 142 migrants, including women and young children, off Dakar.
sources.headline: Canary Islands’ El Hierro declares emergency amid migrant, refugee influx

El ministro de Política Territorial y Memoria Democrática, Ángel Victor Torres, y el presidente de Canarias, Fernando Clavijo, en una imagen de archivo.

El Gobierno ha convocado el próximo martes al presidente canario, Fernando Clavijo, a una reunión de la Comisión Interministerial de Inmigración para tratar el fenómeno migratorio en Canarias y, en particular, la situación que se vive en la isla de El Hierro.

La cita se da a conocer después de que este sábado El Hierro haya declarado la emergencia social ante la llegada de nuevos cayucos: 8.000 personas en las últimas cinco semanas. "Entra más gente de la que podemos derivar", ha explicado el presidente del Cabildo, Alpidio Armas, en una entrevista en el Canal 24 Horas de RTVE.

La reunión tendrá lugar antes del Consejo de Ministros y estará presidida presidida por el ministro de Política Territorial y Memoria Democrática, Ángel Victor Torres. A la misma, asistirán de forma extraordinaria el presidente de Canarias, Fernando Clavijo, y el presidente del Cabildo de El Hierro, Alpidio Armas ; además de los miembros de la misma, que son los titulares de Asuntos Exteriores, Unión Europea y Cooperación; Interior; Inclusión, Seguridad Social y Migraciones; Trabajo y Economía Social; Derechos Sociales, Consumo y Agenda 2030; y Juventud e Infancia.

Fuentes del Ministerio de Política Territorial y Memoria Democrática han confirmado esta reunión, que ha avanzado este sábado por la mañana Clavijo en redes sociales tras hablar con el jefe del Ejecutivo en una conversación, según el presidente canario, en la que Sánchez le ha trasladado "la gravedad de la situación que vive El Hierro ante la presión migratoria y el creciente malestar de su población".

En su mensaje, Clavijo recuerda que "Canarias lleva meses reclamando más recursos, planificación y una respuesta coordinada del Estado".

Según el dirigente canario, Sánchez no solo se ha comprometido con él a "convocar de urgencia" la comisión, sino también a reforzar los recursos sanitarios a través de la Secretaría de Estado de Migraciones.

Esa reunión, añade el presidente canario, "debe servir para acordar entre ambos gobiernos y los ministerios competentes un plan de actuación conjunto, con medidas concretas, responsables y plazos de ejecución", porque "no podemos seguir actuando únicamente cuando la situación se agrava".

También le ha trasladado a Pedro Sánchez que ha solicitado reuniones urgentes con la presidenta de la Comisión Europea, Ursula von der Leyen , y con el comisario europeo de Interior y Migración, Magnus Brunner, porque "Canarias no puede seguir afrontando prácticamente en solitario una situación que exige la implicación del Estado y de Europa".

"></img><p>El ingeniero de Caminos <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-04/el-colegio-de-ingenieros-de-caminos-alerta-del-alto-numero-de-incidencias-en-la-linea-madrid-sevilla.html" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-04/el-colegio-de-ingenieros-de-caminos-alerta-del-alto-numero-de-incidencias-en-la-linea-madrid-sevilla.html">Iñaki de Barrón</a> (Zaragoza, 70 años) observa <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-05/lzb-ertms-y-cdi-113-200-una-semana-descifrando-los-17-minutos-del-accidente-de-urda.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-05/lzb-ertms-y-cdi-113-200-una-semana-descifrando-los-17-minutos-del-accidente-de-urda.html">el siniestro ferroviario de Urda</a> (Toledo) desde una posición de larga experiencia en el ferrocarril. Le respaldan 34 años de gestión en Renfe, hasta 2021; haber sido una figura relevante en la Unión Internacional de Ferrocarriles, y su cargo de presidente de la Comisión de Investigación de Accidentes Ferroviarios (CIAF) hasta julio, teniendo como última encomienda de calado el análisis del accidente de Adamuz (Córdoba), también en la línea de alta velocidad Madrid-Sevilla. Actúa ahora como vocal del Colegio de Ingenieros de Caminos, en cuya sede de Madrid se realiza esta entrevista el pasado jueves, y aconseja una auditoría exhaustiva en la alta velocidad tras <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-04/el-colegio-de-ingenieros-de-caminos-alerta-del-alto-numero-de-incidencias-en-la-linea-madrid-sevilla.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-04/el-colegio-de-ingenieros-de-caminos-alerta-del-alto-numero-de-incidencias-en-la-linea-madrid-sevilla.html">estimar en 10.000 millones</a> el esfuerzo necesario en mantenimiento para los próximos diez años. Esa cifra no solo multiplica las previstas por el Gobierno (que van de los 435 millones presupuestados en 2025 a los 628 para 2030), sino que excluye el gasto imprescindible para poner al día la red convencional que usan los trenes de Cercanías y mercancías: ahí el problema es “peor”, advierte. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-08/inaki-barron-el-ferrocarril-tiene-mucho-que-envidiar-en-seguridad-al-modo-aereo-sobre-todo-en-entrenamiento.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p><img src="https://imagenes.elpais.com/resizer/v2/OQPGEVWTCZGNRDCBVQRKS2SMIE.jpg?auth=60984cebd9e4d449ec20d3c420561535d1677f8104f3dafdfcef5554c2ce2aca" width="2640" height="3960" alt="Iñaki Barrón, antes de la entrevista. "></img>

sources.body:
La Agencia Estatal de Seguridad Ferroviaria registra anualmente los precursores de accidentes en España Getty | DiseñoRTVE

Hay un tramo de unos nueve kilómetros de la línea de alta velocidad Madrid-Sevilla que llama la atención. A la altura de la localidad cordobesa de Palma del Río, entre los puntos kilométricos 388.2 y 396.8, se han detectado hasta 11 deformaciones de la vía en los últimos años. En la misma línea, en el entorno de la estación madrileña de la Puerta de Atocha, se han producido hasta nueve rebases de señal en apenas kilómetro y medio. Estos dos puntos concentran un tercio de los 62 precursores de accidentes registrados por la Agencia Estatal de Seguridad Ferroviaria (AESF) entre 2017 y 2024, el último año con datos disponibles desglosados por tipo de red y línea. Es el primer AVE que se inauguró en España y la línea donde dos accidentes -el de Adamuz y Urda - han dejado 115 víctimas mortales en apenas nueve meses.

Los precursores son fallos -como la deformación de una vía, la rotura de un carril o el rebase de una señal- que bajo determinadas circunstancias pueden contribuir a que se produzca un siniestro. "Es una señal de alerta, una situación que no ha terminado provocando un accidente, pero nos indica que hay un riesgo que hay que analizar", explica Fernando Minaya , vocal del Colegio de Ingenieros de Obras Públicas y perito judicial, quien subraya por este motivo la importancia de su registro.

En la red ferroviaria de alta velocidad se han registrado 207 precursores entre 2017 y 2024 . La mitad de ellos (103) son deformaciones de vía, seguidos de los rebases de señal (78), roturas de carril (25) y un fallo de señalización, según el detalle facilitado por la AESF a través de una petición de transparencia tras el accidente de Adamuz.

El crecimiento en los dos últimos años hasta rozar los 50 incidentes anuales se debe fundamentalmente a los rebases de señal, que han pasado de estar por debajo de la decena a dispararse hasta los 24 fallos en cada uno de los dos últimos ejercicios con registros.

Un rebase se produce cuando una parte de un tren supera un punto a partir del cual no tiene autorización de movimiento ya sea porque el tren rebasa ligeramente una señal -un semáforo, por ejemplo- pero se detiene antes de alcanzar un punto de peligro o porque el tren invade un cantón donde puede haber otro convoy.

Minaya considera una "barbaridad" el aumento de los rebases e insiste en que no se puede "reducir este problema únicamente al factor humano" porque un maquinista interprete mal una señal o porque haya una pérdida de comunicación con el centro de control. " El sistema ferroviario se basa en barreras. Cuando falla una, hay otra que se tiene que activar , y si falla esa segunda barrera, tiene que activarse una tercera y deben funcionar de forma coordinada", explica. Si están aumentando de manera "tan significativa", añade, no solo hay que preguntarse por qué se producen, sino "qué está ocurriendo con esas barreras".

El siguiente mapa localiza la mayoría de los precursores a lo largo de la red de alta velocidad española. Puede consultar el detalle de cada incidente.

stories.headline: Barcelona police arrest 50 people in investigation into alleged migrant-entry scheme

sources.body:
Els Mossos d'Esquadra han detingut 50 membres d'una organització criminal dedicada presumptament a facilitar l'entrada irregular de persones migrants.

Segons la investigació –la més gran feta fins ara per la policia catalana en l'àmbit de la immigració irregular–, la xarxa captava ciutadans vulnerables del Pakistan que, a canvi de pagaments de fins a 30.000 euros , se'ls facilitava documentació i contracte de feina perquè vinguessin a Catalunya.

Els investigadors han detingut 7 presumptes membres de l'organització criminal i també 43 empresaris que cobraven per tramitar irregularment contractes ficticis per facilitar l'entrada dels migrants.

La policia ha constatat que, en molts casos, les persones no arribaven a treballar mai, i en altres ocasions ho feien en condicions precàries o properes a l'explotació.

La investigació ha constatat que l'organització assumia totes les fases del procés, des de captar les víctimes i fer d'intermediaris amb empresaris, fins a tramitar els expedients i formalitzar els contractes de treball.

Entre març del 2022 i juliol del 2023 la xarxa hauria tramitat un total de 224 expedients de contractació en origen, dels quals 108 van obtenir una resolució favorable.

Només pels 108 expedients favorables analitzats, els investigadors estimen que l'organització podria haver obtingut més de 3,2 milions d'euros .

Les persones que es trobaven al Pakistan abonaven quantitats que podien arribar als 30.000 euros per obtenir el visat, la documentació administrativa, l'empadronament i el contracte de treball necessari per accedir al territori estatal.

Però, a més, la xarxa també captava persones que ja es trobaven a Espanya en situació administrativa irregular i a qui cobraven fins a 8.000 euros per accedir a contractes de treball simulats que els permetessin iniciar el procés de regularització.

Els empresaris participants també percebien contraprestacions econòmiques per facilitar les empreses o la documentació laboral requerida per als expedients.

En total s'han identificat 12 presumptes membres de la xarxa, que assumien funcions de captació, intermediació, gestió documental i coordinació de les diferents fases necessàries per tramitar els expedients fraudulents. Set han estat detinguts.

Els Mossos han identificat també 62 empresaris vinculats a activitats econòmiques diverses, entre les quals hi ha establiments d'alimentació, negocis de restauració, empreses de reformes o tallers mecànics i n'ha detingut 43.

Dels 50 detinguts, tres han entrat ja a la presó .

La majoria de les detencions s'han fet a Barcelona, l'Hospitalet de Llobregat, Badalona, Santa Coloma de Gramenet i Sant Adrià de Besòs, així com a Sabadell, Terrassa, Vic, Sant Boi de Llobregat i Sant Vicenç dels Horts.
sources.headline: 50 detinguts en l'operació més gran contra una xarxa que facilitava l'entrada irregular de migrants

stories.headline: Barcelona approves creation of public company to rehabilitate 4,000 Besòs-Maresme homes

sources.body:
Ja hi ha les bases per crear una societat conjunta entre l'Ajuntament de Barcelona i la Generalitat , Impulsem Futur Besòs-Maresme, per rehabilitar centenars de pisos amb greus deficiències al barri del Besòs i el Maresme , al districte de Sant Martí de Barcelona.

Així ho ha aprovat aquest dijous el ple de l'Ajuntament de Barcelona . La creació d'aquesta societat conjunta, però, xoca amb l'aparició d'una proposta municipal d'enderrocar 1.800 habitatges del barri, un escenari que no s'havia plantejat mai i que ha encès els ànims.

El Besòs-Maresme és un dels barris amb la renda per càpita més baixa de la ciutat i amb un dels índexs més alts de vulnerabilitat. Durant anys, ha vist passar diversos plans de regeneració fallits, fins al punt de reclamar la implicació de la Generalitat.

La nova proposta municipal apareix a la Memòria Econòmica amb l'objectiu d' accelerar la regeneració del barri . Una part del document contempla la possibilitat de tirar a terra un dels habitatges amb "deficiències molt severes i que en requereixen la substitució".

I recull que per tirar endavant aquesta possibilitat cal aprovar una modificació del Pla General Metropolità . En cas que no s'aprovi aquesta modificació, el document recull la possibilitat de rehabilitació integral dels 1.800 habitatges amb patologies molt severes.

Tot i que la Memòria presenta l'enderroc com una opció, l'Ajuntament de Barcelona diu que en cap cas s'ho planteja i argumenta que "la creació d'una societat mercantil pública requereix diversos informes que han d'analitzar totes alternatives possibles. Això no vol dir, però, que es plantegi optar per l'enderroc" .

L'Ajuntament i la Generalitat aposten per la rehabilitació.

El mateix document reconeix que en només quatre anys s'han rehabilitat 192 habitatges, i que amb el ritme actual es trigaria uns 40 anys a regenerar tot el barri.

I reconeix que l'Institut Municipal d'Urbanisme no té prou recursos per dur a terme aquesta transformació.

Per això, aposta per la nova empresa mixta Ajuntament-Generalitat, amb un pressupost de 415 milions 265 aportats per l'Ajuntament i 150 per la Generalitat per rehabilitar uns 4.000 habitatges .

El sol fet que s'hagi plantejat sobre paper la possibilitat d'enderrocar bona part del barri ha creat malestar i ha fet que l'associació SOS Besòs es plantegi demanar que la Fiscalia obri una investigació sobre la gestió municipal des del 2019 fins ara.

Teresa Pardo , representant de l'entitat veïnal, diu que volen saber "per què no han tirat endavant els projectes que ja estaven redactats".

I ha dit que "aquí gairebé no han aterrat els ajuts europeus dels Next Generation " i es pregunta "per què s'han articulat solucions a edificis que porten temps apuntalats".

També ha afegit que " no hi ha hagut alternatives de reallotjament quan els bombers han hagut de fer fora els veïns de casa seva":

Hem demanat a les forces polítiques suport jurídic per demanar a la Fiscalia que obri una investigació.

Teresa Pardo es queixa que ara surti aquesta proposta d'enderrocament, quan el 2024, assegura, es negava que hi hagués risc al barri.
sources.headline: Llum verda a la creació d'una empresa pública per rehabilitar 4.000 pisos del Besòs-Maresme

stories.headline: Rodalies and southern regional trains face delays amid shortages of drivers and trains

sources.body:
Nou dia de problemes a Rodalies, amb cancel·lacions de trens i retards importants a diverses línies, que en alguns casos superen la mitja hora.

Segons Renfe, la incidència és de caràcter operatiu i ha provocat falta de trens i de maquinistes . Al darrere hi ha la implantació d'uns nous horaris de treball , després que Semaf, el sindicat majoritari de maquinistes, trenqués l'acord que mantenia amb l'empresa.

Sense aquest pacte, Renfe ha establert nous torns, amb canvis en els horaris de treball i descans. La modificació ha afectat especialment els maquinistes que havien de començar la jornada lluny del seu domicili i que, en alguns casos, no han pogut incorporar-se al servei amb normalitat.

La incidència arriba pocs dies abans de les dues jornades de vaga convocades per Semaf per a la setmana que ve.

R1, R2 Nord, R2 Sud i R4: acumulen retards d'entre 20 i 30 minuts, que en alguns casos poden ser superiors.

R3 : es manté el servei alternatiu per carretera entre Ripoll i Puigcerdà.

R7 : continua interrompuda. Renfe recomana utilitzar els trens de l'R4 fins a Cerdanyola del Vallès i consultar els serveis alternatius de transport.

R13 (Regionals) : registra demores que poden superar els vint minuts de mitjana. També es manté el servei alternatiu per carretera entre Lleida-Pirineus i la Plana de Picamoixons.
sources.headline: Retards a Rodalies i Regionals del sud per una "incidència operativa" per falta de maquinistes i trens

stories.headline: Barcelona’s Tramvia Blau returns for a static display marking its 125th anniversary

sources.body: Una unitat del Tramvia Blau ha reaparegut a la via del seu recorregut tradicional, a l’ avinguda del Tibidabo . Tot i que molts nostàlgics l’haurien volgut veure de nou en marxa, només s’ha pogut exhibir estàtic tot just on començava el trajecte, a la part baixa de l’avinguda. Romandrà durant tot el cap de setmana per commemorar el 125è aniversari d’aquest emblemàtic mitjà de transport de la ciutat, després que es cancel·lés la setmana anterior en senyal de dol per l’ accident ferroviari de Toledo . El 14 i 15 de novembre també s’obrirà al públic el taller , al carrer de Bosch i Alsina. Descobrir-ne els secrets Aquest dissabte al matí s’ha fet una xocolatada popular, hi ha hagut figurants vestits d’època i TMB ha expedit un bitllet commemoratiu del 125è aniversari . Els visitants i curiosos han tingut l’oportunitat de pujar a la unitat número 5 i descobrir-ne tots els detalls que amaga. Bancs i revestiments de fusta, làmpares de disseny, la botzina accionada amb el peu, el tròlei mòbil, el fre accionat amb un timó o un cartell curiós en què s’indica expressament “Està prohibit escopir”. També et pot interessar Les senyores del Tramvia Blau, set anys després i el mateix crit: “Salvem el tramvia” Bàsics 2 minuts de lectura Afloren els records Per a alguns ha estat la primera ocasió per pujar-hi, però per a altres ha estat una oportunitat per recordar vells temps. És el cas d’un avi que hi ha portat el seu net petit: “Vaig venir amb el meu pare quan era petit , hi vaig portar el meu fill; després, el net de 17 anys, i ara em faltava aquest”. Declara amb emoció que tenia moltes ganes d’aquest dia, però alhora admet que li sap greu que no funcioni . “És una tradició que s’ha de conservar”, ha afegit. Una senyora ha refrescat la memòria en veure el tramvia: “N’he recordat el so , estaria bé que fes una mica de ruta”. Com no podia ser d’una altra manera, també s’hi han deixat veure els aficionats al món del ferrocarril. “S’ha de recuperar el tramvia . Jo de petit l’he vist, però la gent jove no l’ha vist”, ha dit un d’ells. La unitat número 5 del Tramvia Blau, a l’avinguda del Tibidabo Exposició sobre la seva història A més a més, durant tot el mes de novembre la ciutadania podrà visitar a l’ Espai Mercè Sala —a l’estació de metro de Diagonal— una exposició que repassa la història completa del Tramvia Blau. S’hi explica el paper cabdal que ha tingut en la transformació del Tibidabo des que va començar a circular el 1901 , així com el seu valor patrimonial i històric per a la ciutat. També et pot interessar AV Avinguda Tibidabo: “Volem donar un futur al nostre passat” Eduard Colldecarrera i Vega 1 minut de lectura El 1971, tots els tramvies de la ciutat van desaparèixer menys el Tramvia Blau. A partir del 1981, TMB va assumir-ne la gestió i el manteniment. El 28 de gener del 2018 va fer l’ últim recorregut i, des d’aleshores, la tornada al servei s’ha fet esperar, tot i que Collboni es va comprometre a iniciar el procés el 2027 . El 23 de maig del 2023, set unitats del tramvia van ser declarades Bé Cultural d’Interès Nacional , de manera que s’ha de garantir la preservació dels vehicles. També et pot interessar La recuperació del Tramvia Blau s’allarga, com a mínim, fins al 2027 Laura Siles Ruth Rodríguez Porta 2 minuts de lectura
sources.headline: El Tramvia Blau reapareix a l’avinguda del Tibidabo pel seu 125è aniversari

sources.body:
Uno de los guardias de seguridad del Tramvia Blau

El Tramvia Blau está celebrando sus 125 años. Transports Metropolità de Barcelona (TMB) ha traído este fin de semana a la avenida del Tibidabo un vagón del 1904 que se incorporó a este servicio en 1934 procedente de la línea de Vallvidriera. Estén atentos a la agenda de actos de estos días.

Cientos de personas no desaprovecharon este sábado la oportunidad de subirse a este pedazo de nuestra historia y hacerse un selfie con el cartel que dice que está prohibido escupir a su espalda. Últimamente por el Raval varios vecinos cuelgan carteles que recuerdan que no está permitido escupir por la calle.

Sí, la cola para subirse a este vagón que no se mueve llega hasta la clínica del Doctor Manchón, pero dan chocolate caliente con melindros gratis ¡todos los que puedas tomarte! No hacen preguntas, te vuelven a servir sin más. Y los niños se entretienen a ritmo de charlestón gracias a unos músicos vestidos de época.

Además, el sarao está amenizado por Nautilus, unos cuantos jubilados sin ánimo de lucro y un fondo de armario espectacular que el otro día participaron en Málaga en una exposición inmersiva del Titanic recreando su última cena. Tienen prendas de entre 1800 y 1950 y según la ocasión se ponen unas y otras...

“Nos pagan el viaje, la comida... es un hobby caro”. “Este abrigo tiene un siglo”. “Mire que suave es este sombrero de copa de piel de foca”. “Este traje tiene más de cien horas de costura. Los de mujer se conservan peor y has de hacértelos”. “A París fuimos así en el AVE ¡y la gente cuando levantaba la vista del móvil...!”.

También procuran respetar los ademanes de la época que representan. A veces, cuando se aburren, se dan una vuelta por el paseo de Gràcia de esta guisa. En verdad se trata de otra forma de conservar el otro patrimonio, de preservar al cotidianidad de otros tiempos.

La ciudadanía está encantada. “¿No van a poner el tranvía en la Diagonal? que recuperen el Blau de una vez”. “Mi abuelo me subía los sábados ¡era una fiesta!”. Lo que pasa es que su rehabilitación y la reforma de la avenida del Tibidabo ronda los 46 millones de euros. Así que se demora.

“¡Bo ha venido!”. Bo es un jabalí, una de las mascotas del parque de atracciones del Tibidabo. Es todo tan entrañable en este lado tan alto de Barcelona que le dan a uno ganas de filetear a Bo y montar una barbacoa. ¿ Y entonces qué pintan esos vigilantes pertrechados a lo Robocop?”. Llevan hasta chalecos antipuñaladas...

No, no es que TMB desconfíe de los amantes del patrimonio, de los niños que se entretienen con el charlestón y de las familias aficionadas al chocolate con melindros. Es que quiere asegurarse de que los grafiteros no vengan a tatuar el Tramvia Blau con sus aerosoles. De ahí el tamaño de las porras de los vigilantes.

No es una paranoia. Con motivo de la última exposición de vagones históricos del metro, las pasadas Navidades, TMB desplegó un ejército. Además, la noche anterior el cine Texas se llenó con el estreno de  F üu di Frei  (Sentirse libre), un documental sobre gente que grafitea trenes en Suiza, sobre el peligro, la adrenalina y estar en contra de casi todo.
sources.headline: El Tramvia Blau de Barcelona también se blinda ante los grafiteros
